subject: Biotechnology
title: HLA and Drug Hypersensitivity
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on HLA and Drug Hypersensitivity.

hook.text: Abacavir treats HIV — but in 5% of patients it triggers a life-threatening allergic reaction. One gene test prevents it.

buildup.text: HLA-B*57:01 presents abacavir fragments to T cells as if they were foreign — triggering a massive immune attack.

discovery.text: Mandatory HLA testing before prescribing abacavir virtually eliminated hypersensitivity reactions — a pharmacogenomic triumph.

twist.text: Carbamazepine and HLA-B*15:02 cause Stevens-Johnson syndrome — severe skin blistering, especially common in Southeast Asians.

climax.text: Pre-prescription HLA testing is now standard for several drugs — genotype before the first pill.

punchline.text: One test, zero deadly reactions — HLA screening is pharmacogenomics at its best.

quiz.question: How does HLA-B*57:01 cause abacavir hypersensitivity?
options: It prevents the body from absorbing abacavir properly
It presents abacavir fragments to T cells, triggering an immune attack as if they were foreign
It converts abacavir into a toxic metabolite in the liver
